svg.text: Approval-gated AI operations agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, operating across AWS accounts

g.text: Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate (ARM64) · auto scaling

foreignObject.div: Operators sign in with Amazon Cognito managed login (OIDC, optional MFA). Cognito groups map to roles (viewer, operator, SRE, admin) and a protected attribute sets the tenant.
The browser connects over HTTPS to Amazon CloudFront, where AWS WAF applies managed rule groups and rate limiting.
CloudFront reaches an internal Application Load Balancer through a VPC origin. The load balancer has no public address and also requires a secret origin header.
The ALB routes to the console (React + FastAPI) on Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate in private subnets across two Availability Zones. Each chat turn runs as a background job with a heartbeat.
The console signs every request. Chat goes to the planner runtime on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, the only component that talks to a model; its IAM role is read-only.
Amazon Nova Micro routes the request to one or two tool domains; Amazon Nova Pro reasons and calls tools. Read-only calls run immediately; listings are complete or flagged as incomplete.
Every call that would change something is intercepted by the approval gate and stored as a pending action in Amazon DynamoDB. Nothing changes, and the planner's role could not change it anyway.
A second person approves the card. The executor runtime, which has no model, replays the stored call at most once and records the result in the audit log and conversation memory.
In member accounts the planner assumes a read-only role and the executor a change role, each with an ExternalId. Only the tenant's registered accounts are allowed.
Every hour, Amazon EventBridge Scheduler runs the learning-loop task, which writes resolved tickets to Amazon S3 and syncs the Bedrock knowledge base (S3 Vectors) used for future escalations.
Logs and embedded metrics go to Amazon CloudWatch (dashboard and alarms); alarms notify by email through Amazon SNS.
scripts/deploy.py, or the GitHub pipeline (staging, evaluation gate, approval, production), deploys two AWS CloudFormation stacks; AWS CodeBuild builds the ARM64 console image into Amazon ECR.
